record.original_question: Is the space of homogenous quasimorphisms on Diff0 (D2 , ∗) one dimensional?

evidence.quote: Question 3.2. Is the space of homogenous quasimorphisms on Diff0 (D2 , ∗) one dimensional?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D^2$ denote the closed 2-disk and let $* \in D^2$ be a fixed basepoint (for instance an interior point). Let $\mathrm{Diff}_0(D^2, *)$ denote the identity component of the group of orientation-preserving $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $D^2$ that fix the basepoint $*$ (and, where applicable, restrict to the identity on $\partial D^2$).

A function $\phi : G \to \mathbb{R}$ on a group $G$ is called a quasimorphism if there is a constant $D \geq 0$ such that
$$|\phi(gh) - \phi(g) - \phi(h)| \leq D \quad \text{for all } g, h \in G.$$
A quasimorphism $\phi$ is called homogeneous if $\phi(g^n) = n\,\phi(g)$ for every $g \in G$ and every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Let $Q(G)$ denote the real vector space of homogeneous quasimorphisms on $G$, and let $H(G) \subset Q(G)$ denote the subspace of homomorphisms $G \to \mathbb{R}$.

Question: Is the quotient space $Q(\mathrm{Diff}_0(D^2, *)) / H(\mathrm{Diff}_0(D^2, *))$ (equivalently, the space of homogeneous quasimorphisms modulo homomorphisms) one-dimensional? More precisely, is $\dim_{\mathbb{R}} Q(\mathrm{Diff}_0(D^2, *)) = 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question about the dimension of the space of homogeneous quasimorphisms on $\mathrm{Diff}_0(D^2,*)$. Related work shows that for area-preserving and Hamiltonian diffeomorphism groups of surfaces the space of homogeneous quasimorphisms is infinite-dimensional, but the smooth (non-area-preserving) pointed disk case appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Entropy and quasimorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: There are infinitely many linearly independent homogeneous quasimorphisms on Diff(S, area), on Diff_0(S, area) and on Ham(S).
status_evidence.claim: Infinite-dimensional results exist for area-preserving cases, but the smooth pointed-disk case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Quasimorphism - Wikipedia
status_evidence.claim: Standard definitions used in formulating the problem; no resolution of this specific dimension question.
